visuals.title: Quiz
visuals.text: Five questions. Answer along on the cards below the transcript, then hear Marco's answers.

quiz.pause_at: Pause here if you want to think it through
quiz.answers_at: Answers. One: net income down fifteen

questions.q: Tax at 25%. Depreciation goes up by 20. What happens to net income and cash?
questions.explain: Pre-tax income falls 20 and tax falls 5, so net income falls 15. Add back the 20 of depreciation: cash rises by the 5 of tax saved.
questions.explain_at: Depreciation is tax-deductible, so the government effectively absorbs a quarter

questions.q: A company borrows 50 in cash. What happens?
questions.explain: Borrowing isn't income, so the income statement doesn't move: financing +50, cash up 50, debt up 50.
questions.explain_at: Then you just skip it. Borrowing a hundred

questions.q: It pays 10 of dividends. Where does that show up?

options.text: An expense of 10 on the income statement

questions.explain: Dividends aren't an expense. They're cash paid to the owners: financing −10, cash down 10, retained earnings down 10.
questions.explain_at: Retained earnings goes up by net income, and down by any dividends paid

questions.q: It buys 30 of inventory with cash. What happens to cash from operations?

options.text: No change, it's an asset swap

questions.explain: Inventory is an asset that went up, so cash from operations falls by 30. It isn't an expense yet, so net income doesn't move.
questions.explain_at: Changes in receivables, inventory and payables come from working capital

questions.q: Where does net income end up on the balance sheet?

options.text: Cash, at the end of the year

questions.explain: Net income flows into retained earnings, inside equity, which is how the balance sheet keeps balancing.
questions.explain_at: Net income also flows into the balance sheet, into retained earnings
